scope: Independent local capture/code analysis and one read-only installed-source SSH probe. No production requests, writes, restarts, configuration changes or load tests.

abort_claim.verdict: The 11 recorded AbortErrors follow the client timeout policy; their underlying cause is not identified.
abort_claim.code_evidence: The measured GET owns an AbortController with a 3000 ms timer. Final shutdown sets done before aborting and suppresses further error records.
abort_claim.failure_timing_limit: Three failed resources in the partial dump last about 3 s and have zero detailed request/response/connect fields. Such incomplete failure timing does not prove that no request reached the server.

keepalive_claim.configuration_evidence: Active CLI and whitelisted UVICORN_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE/HTTP/LOOP process environment have no overrides. Effective default is inferred, not read from the running Config object.
keepalive_claim.verified_semantics: Installed httptools protocol arms the timer after response completion if no pipelined request waits, and cancels it on newly received request data. It is not timed from the previous browser request start. It does not expire an unfinished SSE response.
keepalive_claim.verdict: Five-second keepalive plus five-second polling is a plausible reuse/idle-expiry race under variable tunnel delay. It does not prove the 11 aborts or that about half of all polls retried.

partial_resource_timing.selection: Eight consecutive completed periodic resources after load and before the next abort sequence, browser startTime in [1507000,1543000) ms; a selected diagnostic interval, not all polls.
partial_resource_timing.interpretation: Four slow responses have new local connections and about 293–336 ms before requestStart; four fast responses show reused connections. This supports connection involvement in that interval. The connection is to local port19000; these fields neither separate SSH channel/droplet-side setup nor enumerate retries.

clock_review.GET_stamp: X-Ghost-API-Time-Ns is sampled after get_snapshot performs Redis GET, parsing, clock binding and freshness/eligibility checks, before Response construction (ghost_twap_api.py lines112–127). It is not handler entry.
clock_review.SSE_browser_stamp: The ghost callback samples performance.now after its initial guards. It is callback handling time, not TCP arrival, rendering or trade execution.
clock_review.bound_assumptions: A constant server-wall minus browser-performance offset, nonnegative elapsed paths, and the header clock lying between captured fetch start and body completion. Clock drift/jumps require wider or time-local bounds.
clock_review.interpretation: Under those assumptions, slow-response excess is mainly before the post-lookup header timestamp. That includes browser/tunnel/network/server admission/handler/Redis/parser work; it cannot isolate before-handler delay or give exact one-way latency. Descriptive fast/slow cuts are not a formal bimodality test. Marginal median stages need not sum to median full duration.

slow_client_claim.verdict: A 64 KiB cumulative-output limit and proven slow-client eviction are unsupported.
slow_client_claim.constant_actual_use: Incoming request-body buffer: on_body appends to cycle.body and pauses reads above this limit. It does not cap outgoing SSE.
slow_client_claim.write_semantics: Uvicorn waits on flow.drain when transport pause_writing is active, then writes bytes. High/low marks apply to pending transport output, not cumulative bytes sent. CPython fallback defaults to64/16KiB; uvloop is installed, and active transport thresholds were not measured. Kernel, SSH and browser buffers add separate buffering.
slow_client_claim.send_deadline: The application gives each ASGI send 2000 ms. Success can mean acceptance into transport buffers, not browser consumption; this is no end-to-end deadline.
slow_client_claim.probe_limit: A fetch response left unread by JavaScript may still be buffered by the browser/network stack. No write-buffer occupancy, pause_writing, send-timeout close or slow-client disconnection was measured.
slow_client_claim.supported_conclusion: Normal EventSource delivery continued during the bounded load interval. Slow-client eviction and lossless flow were not established.

report_wording: The client recorded 11 three-second GET aborts. A short post-load sample associated slower GETs with new local connections; the five-second Uvicorn idle timeout is a plausible contributor, but request-level retry/close traces were not collected and causality remains unresolved. The API timestamp is post-lookup, and the slow-consumer exercise did not prove transport backpressure or eviction.

primary_sources.supports: Failed fetches may expose only start/end timing; resource timing is client-side.
Transport high/low marks control pause/resume; defaults are implementation-specific.
